The wicked man who slanders yoga, or the ancestors and grandfathers, / or the masters of yoga, or the practice of yoga;
or the rogue who delights in reviling the Vedas, social classes, life stages, and sacrifices, / the atheist, and the rationalist sceptic—every such person reaches that [hell]. / All this has been spoken truly by me; of this there is no doubt.
Thus tormented there, bound by the fruits of their own deeds, / they are subsequently born, bound by the remainder [of their karma], in the wombs of worms.
The wise, sensible person who, having reflected, constantly listens to this [account], free from greed, delusion, and sorrow, / with his mind impelled by divine law, goes to heaven alone and never enters that [hell].
Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, named Mahāpadma, in the description of hells in the Skandapurāṇa.
Hereafter I shall describe once again the Raurava hell, / wherein living beings, helpless, are bound by their own karma.

Then, released once more, he falls into high precipices. / Those men who are drinkers of liquor and teachers of [false] doctrine go to it:
A father-killer, a mother-killer, a brother-killer, and likewise a guru-killer; / those who delight in disputations against them and revilers of those very people; / a killer of cattle, and a brutally harsh subduer of creatures;
A cutthroat, one who is deceitful in measurement, and one who acts fraudulently by his deeds. // 8.46.10
A younger brother married before his elder, an elder brother unmarried after his younger, one who delights in cremation grounds, / one who cohabits with a twice-married woman's daughter, and one in whose house is a wife's paramour: / all these men go to the hell Raurava.
Whoever hears of this Raurava hell of wrongdoers, the dreadful Raurava, / restrained and self-controlled, shall never go, even in mind, to that exceedingly terrifying Raurava. // 1

7.5.m:
Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, named the Description of Darkness, in the description of hells in the Skandapurāṇa.
Henceforth I will describe the cycle of worldly existence—
how those who have crossed over hell wander in saṃsāra, in brief.
Those evil-doers who have been described by me in the first hell,
due to the residue of their action, are born in the wombs of worms.
Having revolved in the womb of worms for a hundred thousand years,
then they are born again as monkeys and then as hyenas.
Having rotated there for so long, when they are born among cattle,
then there, after precisely a hundred births, from the residue thereafter,
they are born among humans for just as long, without a doubt.
If there they commit no further sin,
then they attain a pure birth once again,
and they do not again reach terrible worldly existence.

Then lions, and snakes, cattle, and afterwards humans.
Now, those evil-doers who were described by me in the fourth [hell]—
all those, having residual [action], are born in the wombs of worms

and for just as long in the womb of an elephant, and among camels and horses.

they are born among worms and insects for twice the number of births;

Then he becomes a crow, and after that a vulture; / and then a bird that eats vomit, and then again an owl. / Again a tree and a shrub, and then indeed he becomes a deer; / then a cow, and also a human who perishes while in the womb.

All this has been told to you in summary in every respect, my son, / as well as the true nature of the hells and the distinction of sequence according to my understanding. / Sanatkumāra said:
He who, being disciplined, listens to this always on festival days, / or recites it properly to twice-borns, is completely freed from all sins.
It brings fortune, brings fame, brings long life, leads to heaven, and accomplishes all aims; / it should be constantly listened to and recited by one desiring prosperity.
This which brings happiness in all aims, firm, of great power, giving a good destination, auspicious, / in accord with the Vedic revelation, should always be firmly retained after studying by a brahmin of composed mind.
